FINDINGS:

**Why merges fail**

1. Every agent inserts its entry at the same place. CHANGELOG.md is newest-first. The preamble ends at line 5, and each new `## vX.Y.Z — date — #id title` block goes in at line 7, directly above the previous newest entry (`## v2.35.5` today). Five branches cut from one commit all add a hunk at the identical anchor. Git sees five insertions at one position. The first merge succeeds, and each later one conflicts. The conflict is textual and unavoidable, even though the entries are logically independent.

2. Each entry carries a version number taken from the current top of the file. Parallel branches pick the same next number. The file already shows the result: `v2.31.0`, `v2.32.0` and `v2.33.0` each appear twice (lines 158/291, 140/234, 132/177). The preamble at lines 3-4 admits the "two circuits" ran into this. Even if the text merged cleanly, the version numbers would still collide. The version is a shared counter that every agent reads and bumps.

3. The file is big and dense, about 92 KB per `docs/tasks/rag-orchestra/research.md`, and entries run to 20+ lines. An agent has to read the top of the file to learn the next version and the format, then edit with surrounding context. That costs several tool calls per task, and more after a conflict.

4. I found no automation, no `.gitattributes` (no merge driver) and no other mention of CHANGELOG in app, scripts or pipelines. The "every task must add an entry" rule is therefore not visible in `CLAUDE.md`, which only links the file at line 3. It probably lives in a role prompt or the orchestrator prompt, which I did not find. Nothing mitigates the shared insertion point.

The repo has already had this problem and fixed it elsewhere. `CLAUDE.md` line 128 says bug reports moved out of the tracked `BUGS.md` because a shared tracked file blocked all merges. Line 209 states the lesson: a store that is written automatically must not share the working tree with Git's lifecycle. The CHANGELOG repeats the `BUGS.md` mistake.

**Cost model**

- Conflicts: with N parallel branches all inserting at the same anchor, the first merge is clean and the other N-1 conflict. Merging them one by one means up to N-1 conflicts per round (4 of 5 here). In the worst case each later merge is re-resolved after the earlier ones, so resolution work grows as roughly N²/2 hunks. Version collisions come on top.
- Tool calls: each conflict needs read, edit and re-merge, about 3-6 calls per conflicted branch. Writing the entry is also expensive, because the agent must read the file head and then edit it.

**Cheapest durable fix: one file per entry, assembled at release time**

- Each task writes `changelog.d/<task-id>.md`, for example `changelog.d/69.md`. This is one `Write` call. It needs no read of CHANGELOG.md and no version number.
- Different filenames never conflict, so conflicts per N branches drop from N-1 to 0. Tool calls per task drop to 1.
- The task id is already unique, since it is assigned by the orchestrator.
- The orchestrator (or a small script run in `merge_worker`) assigns the version and prepends the fragments to CHANGELOG.md in one commit. This is the towncrier / Changesets pattern. Only the orchestrator touches CHANGELOG.md, so version numbers become serial and the duplicate numbering ends.
- Keep the existing `## vX — date — #id title` format inside the fragment. The assembly step then needs no rewrite and the history stays consistent.
- Update the rule text to "add `changelog.d/<id>.md`" in the same place the current rule is stated. Per the `CLAUDE.md` gotcha at line 201, also grep `pipelines/*/prompts/` for the old instruction, or workers will keep following the prompt and not the rule.

**Cheaper stopgap (if you don't want a build step)**

- Add `CHANGELOG.md merge=union` in `.gitattributes`. Git then keeps both sides' lines and never conflicts. Entries can interleave oddly and version numbers still collide, so treat this as a patch and not a durable fix.
- Alternatively, drop version numbers from per-task entries and use only `#id`. Then append at the end of an "Unreleased" section. Appends at the same spot still conflict, so this alone is not enough.

**Not recommended**

- Telling agents to rebase before merge. It adds calls and still conflicts at the same anchor.
- Serializing merges differently. It does not remove the conflicts and contradicts the "maximally parallel" rule at `CLAUDE.md` line 139.

**Caveat:** I didn't check git history, since the snapshot has none. The conflict mechanism comes from the file structure: top insertion and duplicated version headings. I did not reproduce it with real branches.
